config.price_source: Yahoo Finance chart API (adjusted closes), personal research use

caveats: Survivorship bias: companies delisted since 2020 lose their ticker (coverage.no_ticker) or price history (coverage.no_prices), so they are missing. Missing names skew toward bad outcomes, so negative drift is likely understated, but those are also the hardest names to short.
Borrow fees are a flat estimate per size bucket. Hard-to-borrow small caps after offerings can cost far more, or have no shares to borrow at all.
Market-adjusted returns (stock minus index) ignore beta and other factors.
Entry at the day-0 close assumes you can trade at the close; real fills in illiquid names are worse.
Events from the same company or week are not independent, so t-stats are somewhat overstated.
One sample, one period (late 2020 to 2023). A result here is a lead to test out of sample, not a strategy.

t_stat_clustered and t_vs_baseline_clustered cluster by company (CR1) and are reporting only: `significant` uses the unclustered t-stats. The clustered baseline comparison ignores that events and baseline share companies, so it is approximate.
Only the three pre-registered hypotheses in `confirmatory` are confirmatory tests. Everything in results[] is exploratory: a hit there is a lead for a future pre-registered test, not a confirmation.
